newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's Lek falls on NATO, ex-dividend.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's Lek falls on NATO, ex-dividend.

text.p: Slovenian drug maker Lek, which went ex-dividend on Friday, fell 3.36 percent on Monday and traders said selling was encouraged by dimmer prospects for Slovenia joining NATO early.

The United States said on Thursday it did not believe Slovenia was ready to join the North Atlantic Treaty Alliance in the first round of its extension, which may take place in 1999 after talks this summer in Madrid.
"Among Slovenian shares, Lek was the hardest hit by this decision because it was one of the most popular Slovenian firms among foreign investors," said Mateja Gubanec, a trader at "A banka".
"Remaining outside of NATO means international investors will continue to stay away from Slovenia," she added.
By 0840 GMT, Lek was down 750 tolars at 21,600 on volume of 264 shares. Traders said the drop was partly due to the share going ex-dividend.
But they said the stock was likely to bottom out at 21,000 tolars because of the firm's good business results.
